unmapped_findings: Internal inconsistency in S4 tensile data across TB 320 °C and 350 °C: Section 3.3 pairs UTS 1360 MPa/El 10 %/PSE 13,600 MPa·% with 320 °C and UTS 1470 MPa/El 9.1 %/PSE 13,380 MPa·% with 350 °C by word order, yet it then states 'At austenitization at 1150 °C followed by austempering at 350 °C, S4 steel demonstrated a slight improvement in El (10 %)', the conclusion states the best PSE (≈13.6 GPa·%) is at TA 1150 °C/TB 350 °C, and Fig. 7 shows the tallest El column for S4 TA 1150 °C/TB 350 °C. This extraction records the 350 °C condition as UTS 1360 MPa and El 10 % (PSE 13,600 MPa·%; alternative reading UTS 1470 MPa/El 9.1 %/PSE 13,380 MPa·% retained here for transparency).
S4 PSE under optimal conditions (TA 1150 °C, TB 350 °C) ≈ 13.6 GPa·% (13,600 MPa·%), claimed as the best product of strength and elongation among the studied steels.
S4 exhibited the best average and maximum elongation, 10 % and 12 %, at TA 1150 °C and TB 350 °C (slightly higher than S1 and S2).

S4 Ms decreased only marginally from 310 °C (1250 °C austenitization) to 305 °C (1150 °C austenitization); Δ = 5 °C, within experimental scatter, and no clear effect of Ti microalloying on Ms was evident.
For S4, the true lamellar thickness Lt(t) was not significantly influenced by the variations in austenitization temperature and correlated micro-alloying, remaining within the range of 56–58 nm.

The longitudinal alignment of TiMoC precipitates in S4 indicates their formation during the cooling phase after casting, followed by deformation during subsequent hot forming, implying secondary precipitation played a negligible role; an austenitization temperature of 1250 °C was selected to suppress partially the sheaf impingement associated with extremely small prior austenite grain sizes observed at 1150 °C.
S4 austempering temperatures were chosen slightly above the measured Ms (305 °C at 1150 °C austenitization) to promote bainitic transformation while suppressing martensite.

Overall conclusion (iv): Ti + Ni alloying in S4 compensates for its lower C (0.87 wt.%) by elevating elongation and thus PSE, offering the best overall strength–ductility balance among the studied steels.
